steps.claim: Bounded Lipschitz functions of actual E1 tests pass through moving operator outputs
steps.proof: Assume217 full weighted theorem. Let rho_i be an E1 mixed-output net with all slots decreasing to E1 endpoints and rho the limit. For fixed actual E1 a,b and fixed continuous approximants a_k down a,b_l down b, joint weighted continuity implies int(a_k-a)rho_i -> int(a_k-a)rho and similarly for b. Radon increasing-continuous integration makes the limiting errors tend0 as k,l increase. A bounded Lipschitz F on R^2 then gives int f F(a,b)rho_i -> int f F(a,b)rho for every continuous f: replace a,b by fixed-stage continuous approximants with uniform tail L1 control, then weak convergence, then remove the stage. Pole sets of a,b have zero mass for each relevant output by217. No uncountable common full-measure set is claimed.

steps.claim: Diagonal L1 error for the potentials defining winner sets
steps.proof: For continuous approximants u_i down u,v_i down v,m_i=max(u_i,v_i) down m, and remaining slots R_i down R, both rho_i=MA(m_i,R_i) and sigma_i=MA(u_i,R_i) have weighted laws under217. Hence int(u_i-u)rho_i and int(v_i-v)rho_i tend0 by subtracting their moving/fixed weight limits; the same holds for sigma_i. These errors are nonnegative on per-index common finite-value full-measure sets. max endpoint m is actual E1 by closure and energy monotonicity.

For epsilon>0 choose chi_epsilon(d)=0 for d<=0, d/epsilon for0<d<epsilon,1 for d>=epsilon. Continuous strict-winner locality gives int f chi_epsilon(u_i-v_i)rho_i=int f chi_epsilon(u_i-v_i)sigma_i. The diagonal L1 error replaces each cutoff by chi_epsilon(u-v) at negligible cost. The preceding fixed Borel Lipschitz-test lemma passes both integrals to rho=MA(m,R),sigma=MA(u,R). Thus chi_epsilon(u-v)rho=chi_epsilon(u-v)sigma as Radon measures; multiplying Radon measures by bounded Borel functions yields Radon measures on compact Hausdorff spaces via L1 regular approximation. Let sequential epsilon down0 and use ordinary single-measure dominated convergence to obtain restrictions to {u>v}, outside per-measure pole-null sets. Handle {v>u} symmetrically. All literal common -infinity ties lie in pole sets and no arithmetic on infinities occurs.

For epsilon>0 put m=max(u,v-epsilon), rho=MA(m,R),sigma_u=MA(u,R),sigma_v=MA(v,R), all raw massV. Strict locality gives sigma_v({u<v-epsilon})=rho({u<v-epsilon})<=V-rho({u>v-epsilon})=sigma_u({u<=v-epsilon})<=sigma_u({u<v}), with comparisons understood on the common finite-value full-measure sets. Let epsilon decrease sequentially to0. sigma_v({u<v})<=sigma_u({u<v}); repeated slots yield pure comparison. No model support, EP or capacity assumption used.
